newsitem.title: USA: LUKARCO acquires Tengiz share from Chevron.
newsitem.headline: LUKARCO acquires Tengiz share from Chevron.

text.p: LUKARCO, the joint venture formed by Los Angeles-based Atlantic Richfield Co and Russia's LUKOIL, acquired five percent of Chevron Corp's stake in the massive Tengiz oil field, the company said Thursday.
The $200 million purchase, funded mostly by ARCO, gives LUKARCO a stake in the prolific oil field in Kazakstan.
With completion of the sale, ARCO's interest in the field is currently estimated at 50 million barrels of oil.
"This acquisition is a significant step for the LUKARCO joint venture," said ARCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Mike Bowlin.
"The scope of the Tengiz operation is expected to grow steadily over the years, bringing additional reserves for ARCO," he added.
Tengiz is a joint venture of Chevron Corp, Mobil Corp and the government of Kazakstan. Tengiz is currently producing about 160,000 barrels of oil per day.

In addition to the Tengiz/Chevroil development, LUKARCO owns a 12.5 percent interest in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, a multi-party effort to build a 900-mile pipeline from Tengiz to shipping ports in the Black Sea.
LUKARCO was formed by ARCO and LUKOIL in February, 1997 to invest in oil and gas opportunities in Russia and other countries.
LUKOIL owns a 54 percent interest in the joint venture, ARCO 46 percent. Investment in various projects could total $5 billion over 18 years.
